meaning: Titles and reading notes drafted by an AI agent in the register of the paper they annotate. No mathematician has reviewed them.

This is the literal piecewise definition: the axis and off-axis branches have different radial powers. Its hypotheses and uses belong to the accompanying cell estimates.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.entryPai: This pairing conjugates the second argument. The later sumSesq and vecSesq definitions conjugate the first argument.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.turnAdjI: The rational expression is total in Lean, including singular values of k. The admissibility hypotheses in later results control where it serves as an inverse.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellFormu: The polarization coefficient is one half. This convention must agree with the quadratic-form evaluator used by the cell inequality.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayou: The layout validity conditions supply closure under negation where the negative mode must be recovered.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.potential: The fallback makes this selector a total function. The existence and potential identities must come from separate hypotheses or proofs.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.rankOne: The first factor is conjugated, so the quadratic form uses the Hermitian rank-one convention.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.IsSystemIn: This fractional system is fixed at alpha = 501/500. The authors identify the Fractional files as outside the classical paper route.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.CellSystem.inverseSqu: The fallback retains the original remainder and assigns an empty mode set. Finite-support and weighted-L2 facts require the existence branch.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.ProfileDa: The zero fallback alone establishes no weak fractional-power identity; a witness is needed to justify the chosen branch.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.GivenModel.RowData.mi: Positive definiteness is required by IsRowData. This total matrix definition by itself supplies no orthonormality claim.
notes.Breakdown.CellCert.Spectral.certMin: The inserted value one gives an explicit default bound before any stored certificate is applicable.
notes.Breakdown.FractionalBreakdownOnTorus: Only velocity periodicity is imposed on a competing solution; pressure periodicity is absent from this predicate.
notes.Breakdown.IsFractionalSolution: The equation is required at positive times and smoothness includes time zero. Periodicity and a uniform energy bound are added separately by the breakdown predicates.
notes.Breakdown.RotatingFractionalProfileExist: The profile definition itself places no interval restriction on alpha. The breakdown theorems impose 1 < alpha < 5/4.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.IsLocalSquareIntegr: The argument is an arbitrary scalar function; callers pass a square when they require local square-integrability.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.projectedNorm: The set in the infimum explicitly requires F plus Q to lie in L2. Bounds and nonemptiness are separate analytic obligations.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.rowSeminorm: This infimum definition has a different witness condition from projectedNorm: it records the gradient field and the row value.
